newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil mulls fuel exports to Taiwan, S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil mulls fuel exports to Taiwan, S.Korea.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Tuesday it is considering starting low-sulphur fuel oil exports to Taiwan and South Korea following Japan's planned deregulation of oil products exports next week.
"We are examining the feasibility of exporting about 30,000 kilolitres of low-sulphur fuel oil per quarter starting this autumn," a Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said.
He also said fuel oil cargoes are likely to be shipped from Tohoku Oil Co Ltd's 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Sendai on the Pacific coast of northern Japan.
Tohoku Oil, which belongs to the Mitsubishi Oil group, brought a 45,000-bpd fuel oil desulphurisation unit on line in March.

The planned exports are targeted at growing demand for low-sulphur fuel oil at thermal power plants in Taiwan and South Korea, he said, adding that no specific buyers or pricing formulas had been determined.

Starting on July 14, oil product exporters in Japan will only need permission for exports once a year, and can ship their products overseas as many times as they like as long as their accumulated export volume is within the approved figure.
Currently they need to obtain permission from the government each time they plan to export oil products, making it virtually impossible for them to conduct timely export operations.
